payload.technicalDefinitionEn: The stat_buffs parameter key used by the Psyker brain-burst-improved buff template. In this pinned source snapshot, the shared damage calculation reads it on the damage_types.smite branch and multiplies it into damage_multiplier; the pinned Psyker Smite action uses that damage type. This bounded linkage does not resolve other calculation stages or a final damage outcome.

payload.safeSummary: At the fixed upstream commit, the psyker_brain_burst_improved template assigns the code literal 1.5 to stat_buffs[stat_buffs.smite_damage_multiplier]. This evidence supports only the parameter value; downstream damage outcome and runtime application are unverified.

The fixed P1 traits table defines movement_speed values 0.17, 0.18, 0.19, and 0.2; each relevant override has active_duration = 2 (lines 119-143). This supports the literal template parameter only and does not establish actual in-game effect duration.

The talent definition binds the improved brain-burst description's damage format value to smite_damage_multiplier and applies (value - 1) * 100; the pinned talent layout parser renders the percentage with its configured prefix. With source parameter 1.5, the description-format value is 50 percent. This is a code-derived display parameter, not a final damage value; Steam build and localized-description compatibility are unverified.

The fixed trait definition configures movement_speed as a percentage format with a + prefix and its defined tier 1 is 0.17. The pinned trait value parser applies default percentage scaling because no custom value manipulation is configured, so the description-format value is 17 percent. This covers defined tier 1 only, not verified obtainable or game-tested; runtime movement outcome and localized-description compatibility are unverified.

At the fixed upstream commit, the damage calculation checks damage_type == damage_types.smite, reads attacker_stat_buffs.smite_damage_multiplier on that branch, and multiplies the parameter into damage_multiplier (lines 506-514). This records the bounded conditional and multiplication relation only; other calculation stages and final damage are not resolved.

At the fixed upstream commit, the psyker_smite_kill damage target in the psyker_smite action uses damage_types.smite (lines 538-562). This links the selected action to the shared calculation branch condition only; it does not establish runtime resolution or final damage.
The archived analysis identifies a 1.5 Smite damage multiplier and relates it to the Smite-only calculation branch. This is a bounded parameter relationship, not a final-damage result.

The archived analysis records a 3-second normal-charge default when smite_attack_speed=1. Under the described non-target-locked update conditions, charging and Peril can begin before a valid target is acquired. This is a template-level observation, not a universal runtime time.

The archived analysis records a 2-second sticky charge when smite_attack_speed=1, after acquiring a valid lockable target; target-locked mode cannot precharge or switch targets while the lock is maintained. If the target supports Smite stagger, maintaining the lock for 1 second applies one small stagger.

A fresh lock-on charge requires a valid Smite target and uses the normal 3-second default. Chaining can preserve current charge level, while changing the target resets the charge timer. If a target supports Smite stagger, more than 0.25 seconds locked applies one small stagger; these are bounded branch observations, not universal runtime timing.

The archived analysis records a 0.25 base Peril parameter paid only after successful damage; empty casts and misses do not enter that payment branch. The described payment is independent of charge level because the template does not enable use_charge.

Under the archived no-buff assumptions with smite_attack_speed=1, full charge is estimated at 20% Peril; a successful hit adds the 25% base cost for 45% total. Holding full charge for another second adds 9%/s. These are template-based estimates, not measured runtime outcomes.

The fixed trait definition configures movement_speed as a percentage format with a + prefix; its defined tier 2 is 0.18. The pinned trait value parser applies default percentage scaling with no custom value manipulation for this descriptor, so the description-format value is 18 percent. This covers defined tier 2 only, not verified obtainable or game-tested; runtime movement outcome and localized-description compatibility are unverified.

This covers defined tier 4 only, not verified obtainable or game-tested; runtime movement outcome and localized-description compatibility are unverified.

At the pinned source commit, chainaxe_dps_stat selects default_melee_dps_stat with attack-trait endpoints 0.25 and 0.75. The analysis-selected comparison inputs are 60 percent and 80 percent, giving first-stage t values lerp(0.25, 0.75, 0.60) = 0.55 and lerp(0.25, 0.75, 0.80) = 0.65. _resolve_template applies those values to default_light_chainaxe.targets[1].power_distribution.attack raw endpoints 80 and 140, yielding lerp(80, 140, 0.55) = 113 and lerp(80, 140, 0.65) = 119 attack-power points. These are code-derived parameter comparisons only, not an obtainable range or final damage.

At the pinned source commit, chainaxe_armor_pierce_stat selects default_armor_pierce_stat with armored-attack endpoints 0.1 and 0.95. The analysis-selected comparison inputs are 60 percent and 80 percent, giving first-stage t values lerp(0.1, 0.95, 0.60) = 0.61 and lerp(0.1, 0.95, 0.80) = 0.78. _resolve_template applies those values to default_light_chainaxe.targets[1].armor_damage_modifier.attack[armor_types.armored] raw endpoints 1.035 and 1.965, yielding lerp(1.035, 1.965, 0.61) = 1.6023 and lerp(1.035, 1.965, 0.78) = 1.7604 ratios. These are code-derived parameter comparisons only, not an obtainable range or final damage.

At the fixed commit, primary light card is smiter with four smiter displayed_attacks segments; secondary heavy card is linesman with two linesman displayed_attacks segments. weapon_card_data maps primary to light and secondary to heavy. The source role classification is a display summary of displayed_attacks, not the complete action chain; action/profile overrides and per-segment execution remain NOT_IMPORTED.

At the fixed commit, primary light card is tank with two tank displayed_attacks segments; secondary heavy card is smiter with two smiter displayed_attacks segments. weapon_card_data maps primary to light and secondary to heavy. The source role classification is a display summary of displayed_attacks, not the complete action chain; action/profile overrides and per-segment execution remain NOT_IMPORTED.

At commit ba6c148, chainaxe_p1_m1 displays action_left_down_light as the light attack-power row and action_left_heavy as the heavy row. The mapped profiles are default_light_chainaxe with raw target-1 attack endpoints 80 and 140, and heavy_chainaxe with endpoints 150 and 300. default_melee_dps_stat interpolates 0.25 to 0.75: inputs 60% and 80% give t=0.55 and 0.65. The resulting source parameters are light 113 and 119; heavy 232.5 and 247.5 attack-power points. These are profile/mode-scoped parameters, not final HP damage and not values for every displayed segment. The player-facing weapon-info panel exposes the raw power_distribution.attack value through a default display row, with no scalar conversion, and formats it to two decimals; this is a source parameter, not health damage.

At commit ba6c148, chainaxe_armor_pierce_stat applies default_armor_pierce_stat endpoints 0.1 and 0.95; inputs 60% and 80% give t=0.61 and 0.78. The light default_light_chainaxe profile exposes armored/resistant via lerp_1_5 [1.035,1.965] -> 1.6023/1.7604 and super_armor via lerp_0_75 [0.48,1.02] -> 0.8094/0.9012. The heavy_chainaxe profile exposes armored via lerp_0_75 -> 0.8094/0.9012 and super_armor via lerp_0_3 [0.174,0.426] -> 0.32772/0.37056. UI display_type percentage multiplies each raw ratio by 100 and prints two decimals. Only explicit profile armor keys are claimed; values are not final damage.

At commit ba6c148 both chainaxe marks use the linesman stamina template. The player-visible stamina_modifier is the fixed value 4, shown with a plus sign and two decimals as +4.00. The defence slider maps sprint_cost_per_second endpoints 0.25 to 0.75, so inputs 60% and 80% produce first-stage t=0.55 and 0.65, then linesman endpoints 1.25 to 0.75 produce raw 0.975 and 0.925 stamina points per second. The push_cost slider endpoints are 0 to 1, so t=0.60 and 0.80 applied to linesman endpoints 3 to 1 produce 1.8 and 1.4 stamina points. The Source UI formats stamina, sprint cost, and push cost with two decimals; binary floating-point therefore displays sprint cost as 0.97 and 0.93 while raw values remain 0.975 and 0.925, and push cost as 1.80 and 1.40.

At commit ba6c148, chainaxe_sawing_stat maps the displayed light/heavy saw rows to source profile overrides. default_melee_dps_stat endpoints 0.25 to 0.75 give t=0.55/0.65 for the 60%/80% comparison. Profile raw attack-power endpoints yield light active first saw 248/264 (160 to 320), light active final saw 465/495 (300 to 600), ordinary light final saw 173.75/196.25 (50 to 275), heavy active first saw 310/330 (200 to 400), and heavy active final saw 852.5/907.5 (550 to 1100). These are sawing profile attack-power parameters, not health damage or the ordinary light/heavy attack power rows. The player-facing weapon-info panel exposes the raw power_distribution.attack value through a default display row, with no scalar conversion, and formats it to two decimals; this is a source parameter, not health damage.

At commit ba6c148 both marks use smiter_plus dodge and default sprint templates. default_dodge_stat endpoints 0.25 to 0.75 make t=0.55/0.65 at 60%/80%; smiter_plus distance_scale 0.85 to 1.05 yields raw 0.96/0.98, displayed as -4.00%/-2.00% by (value-1)*100. Its diminishing_return_start endpoints 2 to 4 yield raw 3.1/3.3 effective dodges, floored then displayed as 3.00/3.00; speed_modifier stays 1 and displays +0.00%. default_sprint_stat endpoints 0.05 to 0.95 yield t=0.59/0.77; default sprint_speed_mod endpoints -0.5 to 0.5 yield raw ratios 0.09/0.27, displayed as +0.09/+0.27. The UI uses two decimal places and signed formatting for these rows. Hidden movement-curve and non-displayed fields are not included.
